newsitem.title: INDIA: India detains Kashmiris before Pakistan talks.
newsitem.headline: India detains Kashmiris before Pakistan talks.

text.p: Indian police on Friday detained senior leaders of Kashmir's separatist Hurriyat (Freedom) umbrella group hours before Indian and Pakistani diplomats began official talks, witnesses said.

"No Talks on Kashmir without Kashmiris," said one of the placards carried by supporters of Hurriyat chairman Mirwaiz Omar Farooq and his senior colleagues before they were detained in a New Delhi suburb.
The All Party Hurriyat Conference (APHC), the umbrella group comprising some 30 separatist organisations, has opposed bilateral talks between India and Pakistan over the disputed Himalayan region.
An APHC statement said its leaders were planning to hold a peaceful demonstration at New Delhi's Hyderabad House, venue of the official talks, when they were arrested.

Pakistan says Kashmir is a "core issue" to be discussed during the four-day talks between the top diplomats of the two countries which have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain in 1947 over Kashmir.

"The proposed peaceful demonstration...was meant to impress upon the world leadership that the Kashmir issue cannot be solved without the genuine representatives of the people of Jammu and Kashmir," the APHC statement said.
